correctness.rationale: The probability measure and unscaled Fourier phase give T(a+Q)(rθ)=a j0(r)−Q(θ)j2(r); Euclidean polar integration multiplies each spherical average by 4π. Independently recomputed the derivative-product Gram matrix from compactly supported one-dimensional convolutions: the needed radial integrals divided by π are 1/4, 1/20, −1/28 and 11/140. No endpoint distributional masses appear since the even convolution functions are continuous and compactly supported with square-integrable weak derivatives. Fixing a real nonnegative by common phase and writing Q=U+iV gives the exact three nonconstant terms a²(6||U||²+2||V||²)/5, (4a/7)E[U(U²+V²)], and (11/35)E[(U²+V²)²] after division by π². For W=ω^TAω with A symmetric trace-free, E W²=2 tr(A²)/15, E W³=8 tr(A³)/105, and E W⁴=4(tr(A²))²/105. The degree-two projection of W² has matrix (4/7)(A²)_0 by applying the Euclidean Laplacian to the harmonic decomposition of W²; tr(A⁴)=(tr(A²))²/2 verifies its norm factor 2sqrt(5)/7. This bounds both cubic terms, and Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the quartic term. If a>0 and Q≠0, the quadratic inequality forces V=0; the maximal positive cubic moment at fixed trace norm has two equal eigenvalues and one positive simple eigenvalue, precisely the stated positive zonal class. At a=0 equality instead requires U² and V² proportional (or one zero); homogeneous polynomial factorization implies U and V proportional, giving all real harmonics up to complex scalar. The constant case is immediate. Replay: python3 /workspace/review_evidence.py, extension section, exact SymPy radial and latitudinal/azimuthal moment calculations. The code checks arithmetic identities, not sharpness or exhaustive equality; these follow analytically.
